title: nf-core/contaminationqc pipeline parameters
description: Sample contamination, contamination-source attribution, sample identity and non-human (Kraken2) screening for targeted-panel BAM/CRAM files using somalier.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the BAM/CRAM files to analyse.
input.help_text: CSV with a header and the columns `sample`, `bam`, `bai`, and optionally `individual` (patient ID; samples of the same individual are checked for identity and used as anchors) and `batch` (contamination sources are searched within a batch, e.g. a sequencing run). See the usage docs.

somalier_background.description: Optional CSV of previously extracted .somalier files used as additional candidate contamination sources and identity references.
somalier_background.help_text: Columns `sample`, `somalier` and optionally `individual`. Background samples are never reported as receivers. They must have been extracted with the same sites file (e.g. `somalier/extract/` from earlier runs of this pipeline).

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

reference_genome_options.title: Reference genome options
reference_genome_options.description: Reference genome related files and options required for the workflow.

genome.help_text:
If using a reference genome configured in the pipeline using iGenomes, use this parameter to give the ID for the reference. This is then used to build the full paths for all required reference genome files e.g. `--genome GRCh38`. 

See the [nf-core website docs](https://nf-co.re/usage/reference_genomes) for more details.

fasta.description: Path to FASTA genome file the BAM/CRAM files are aligned to.
fasta.help_text: This parameter is *mandatory* if `--genome` is not specified. If you don't have a BWA index available this will be generated for you automatically. Combine with `--save_reference` to save BWA index for future runs.

igenomes_ignore.description: Do not load the iGenomes reference config.
igenomes_ignore.help_text: Do not load `igenomes.config` when running the pipeline. You may choose this option if you observe clashes between custom parameters and those supplied in `igenomes.config`.

igenomes_base.description: The base path to the igenomes reference files

fasta_fai.description: Path to the FASTA index (.fai). Generated if not provided.

sites.description: somalier sites VCF with INFO/AF, matching the genome build and contig naming of the BAMs.
sites.help_text: Sites files for GRCh37/hg19/hg38 are distributed with somalier (https://github.com/brentp/somalier/releases). For targeted panels consider `somalier find-sites` restricted to the panel, or `--panel_bed`.

panel_bed.description: Panel target BED. If provided, sites are restricted to the (padded) targets. Recommended for targeted panels such as TSO500.

bed_pad.description: Pad panel BED intervals by this many bp when restricting sites.

genotyping_options.title: Genotyping and identity options
genotyping_options.description: Genotype calling from somalier allele counts and hom-hom discordance identity checks.

min_depth.description: Minimum depth for a site to be used (somalier recommends >= 20 for cancer samples).

hom_max_af.description: Minor-allele fraction tolerated for homozygous-like calls.

het_min_af.description: Heterozygous call window [x, 1-x] for candidate genotypes.

identity_max_disc.description: Hom-hom discordance at or below which two samples are considered the same individual.

min_identity_sites.description: Minimum number of shared homozygous sites required for identity calls.

attribution_options.title: Contamination source attribution options
attribution_options.description: Mixture model comparing 'candidate sample is the contaminant' against 'an unknown person is the contaminant'.

error_rate.description: Per-read error rate used in the mixture likelihood.

max_eff_depth.description: Cap on the effective depth per site (guards against over-confidence from overdispersion at very high depth).

contam_threshold.description: Flag samples with estimated contamination at or above this fraction.

min_llr.description: Log-likelihood ratio (nat) versus an unknown contaminant required to call a source.

min_margin.description: LLR margin between the best and second-best individual required for an unambiguous source call.

relatedness_flag_threshold.description: Flag sample pairs from different individuals with somalier relatedness above this value (possible contamination or family members).
relatedness_flag_threshold.help_text: The relatedness estimate is noisy on small panels (SD ~0.07 with 1,000 sites), so the default of 0.2 flags ~2 % of unrelated pairs in large cohorts. Raise it (e.g. 0.35) for thousands of samples on a targeted panel.

scaling_options.title: Scaling options
scaling_options.description: Options controlling parallelisation and output size for large cohorts.

attribution_chunk_size.description: Number of receiver samples per source-attribution task.

somalier_anchored_all_pairs.description: Run `somalier contamination` on all ordered sample pairs per batch instead of only within genotype groups (quadratic cost).
somalier_anchored_all_pairs.help_text: By default the anchored (conpair-like) contamination MLE is only computed between samples of the same individual (genotype group), which is all the per-sample summary uses. Enable to populate `somalier_anchored_mle` for every pair in `attribution.pairs.tsv.gz`, as the original script did.

report_top_candidates.description: Keep only the N best candidate sources per receiver in `attribution.pairs.tsv.gz` (0 = all). Recommended for large cohorts, e.g. 25.

max_heatmap_samples.description: Skip the attribution LLR heatmap for batches with more samples than this.

run_kraken2.description: Classify reads with Kraken2 to detect non-human contamination.

kraken2_db.description: Path to a Kraken2 database directory or .tar.gz archive.
kraken2_db.help_text: For thousands of samples use a capped database (e.g. Standard-16 or PlusPF-16) and consider `--kraken2_memory_mapping` with the database on shared storage.

kraken2_reads.description: Classify only read pairs with both mates unmapped (`unmapped`) or all primary reads (`all`).

kraken2_memory_mapping.description: Pass `--memory-mapping` to Kraken2 (avoids loading the database into RAM).

run_bracken.description: Re-estimate abundances with Bracken (requires a Bracken-enabled database).

bracken_read_length.description: Read length for Bracken (must exist in the database's kmer distributions).

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
